review.evidenceBoundary: Seven new actual PostgreSQL cases cover preparation/replay, expired-origin lease through request/effect/materialization, API and human adoption denial, input conflicts, rollback, privileged domain corruption and financial/domain lock contention. The existing final target-rollover case also covers successor preparation and retarget rejection. Three new readiness cases cover the private provenance FK, internal FK trigger and timestamp default. New-origin execution uses real restricted SQL ports with synthetic dispatch evidence. Existing cohorts exercise Redis journeys; this checkpoint does not establish scheduled worker-origin transport or a typed request adapter. Privileged corruption is injected by the disposable database owner, not claimed as a legitimate runtime mutation.

Current installed target/release authority is independent from historical origin lease expiry; successor preparation is allowed and committed preparation never retargets

Exact ACL scrub and namespace-aware readiness cover four new functions, three replaced function bodies, one private table, three explicit triggers, three foreign keys and twelve internal RI triggers
